# mega-smart-context An OpenCode 2.0 plugin that hands context management to the model. Instead of replaying the whole transcript, every request carries the memory document the model wrote, a short verbatim working window, and the current turn.
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/github/package-json/v/megablue/mega-smart-context?style=flat-square)](package.json) [![Topic: opencode-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/topic-opencode--plugin-0e7490.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/topics/opencode-plugin) [![Dependencies: none](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-none-brightgreen.svg?style=flat-square)](package.json) [![Buy me a coffee](https://img.shields.io/badge/buy%20me%20a%20coffee-PayPal-ffdd00.svg?style=flat-square&logo=buymeacoffee&logoColor=black)](https://www.paypal.me/mega3dp)
## What it does - The model writes a **memory document** with the `smart_context` tool — the goal, plan, facts, files, decisions and open threads — and every request starts with it. - An optional **append-only layout** (`contextLayout: "append"`) keeps that document as a checkpoint and appends one accepted delta after each completed turn, so a patch does not rewrite the provider prefix; when the shared pool fills, a due note lists what will leave and the fold waits for the next prompt, keeping the newest `compactKeepTokens` (20k default) of turns and archiving the rest. - A short **verbatim working window** keeps the newest turns exactly as they happened, so nothing in the live tool loop is paraphrased. - When a turn leaves the window it moves to a **gated archive**, kept for `recall` rather than replayed or dropped silently. - **Compaction is owned by the plugin.** When the host makes a checkpoint, the plugin answers with the memory document itself instead of a separate summarization call. - **Subagents are managed independently**, each with its own window and memory, so a child never inherits the parent's context. - `/context` prints the current memory and archive; `/context now` archives pending turns; `/context resume` continues the session without adding a user message or ageing an eviction. ## Requirements - OpenCode 2.0. - Node 22 or newer. The host loads the TypeScript source directly; there is no build step and no runtime dependency. ## Install Project scope (this repository only): ```sh npm run plugin:install:project ``` User scope (every project on this machine): ```sh npm run plugin:install ``` Check what is installed and whether it has drifted from the source tree: ```sh npm run plugin:status ``` Remove the selected scope: ```sh npm run plugin:uninstall ``` Installing copies the shippable files and removing deletes them; editing the source tree does not change an installed copy until you reinstall. OpenCode picks up a re-synced or removed copy at its next load, so restart it only to make that immediate — and always after a *first* install, when the host has not seen the directory yet. > **Do not run this alongside `mega-skillstate`** (or any other plugin that rewrites the context hook). Both rewrite the same request and both may own compaction. Disable the other plugin first. > **Install one scope, not both.** OpenCode reads both discovery roots and keys a plugin by the path it was loaded from, so a user copy and a project copy are two instances of this plugin in a session in that repository: two window passes per request, two owners of compaction, two `/context` commands. Pick user scope to cover every project, or project scope to cover this repository alone. `npm run plugin:status` prints both, so a stray copy is visible there. ## Configure On first run the plugin writes `~/.config/opencode/mega-smart-context.json` with every default and never overwrites it. Layers, most specific last: 1. built-in defaults, 2. the package `options.json`, 3. the host's plugin options, 4. the user file. An unknown key or a wrong type is an error; the plugin refuses to load rather than silently keeping a default. The settings a user normally touches: | Setting | Default | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `enabled` | `true` | master switch | | `contextLayout` | `"snapshot"` | `"snapshot"` rewrites one memory block; `"append"` keeps a checkpoint and appends deltas | | `memoryTokens` | `20000` | cap on the model-authored memory, estimated | | `workingTokens` | `20000` | cap on the verbatim working window, estimated | | `autoArchive` | `true` | archive unhandled evictions instead of dropping them | | `evictionLead` | `1` | new user turns a pending turn is shown before archiving | | `parentArchive` | `true` | let a subagent search its spawning session's archive (`from:"parent"`) | | `expandDigestChars` | `4000` | characters per `expand` page, clamped by `maxResultChars` | | `subagents` | `true` | manage child sessions independently | | `refs` | `true` | allow feature-map references | | `updateCheck` | `true` | ask GitHub once a day for a newer version (one TUI toast per release) | | `sidebar` | `true` | draw the block in the TUI sidebar (`sidebar:false` removes it, keeps the dialog) | | `debug` | `false` | log pass decisions to stderr | | `profiles` | `{}` | named bundles of the session-level settings (see below) | | `modelProfiles` | `{}` | `provider/model` (or `#variant`, or a bare model id) to a profile name | | `defaultProfile` | `""` | the profile an auto session falls back to | Profiles are named bundles of the session-level settings. A session takes, in order, a manual pin, a `modelProfiles` entry for the model in use, `defaultProfile`, or the base config; a manual pin stays until you pick **auto**, whatever model is used later. ```json { "profiles": { "lean": { "memoryTokens": 10000, "workingTokens": 12000, "maxResultChars": 2000 }, "deep": { "memoryTokens": 30000, "workingTokens": 60000, "archiveMaxChars": 200000 } }, "modelProfiles": { "opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free": "lean", "gpt-5": "deep" }, "defaultProfile": "lean" } ``` A profile may set only the session keys (`contextLayout`, `memoryTokens`, `workingTokens`, `charsPerToken`, `evictionLead`, `autoArchive`, `archiveMaxTurns`, `archiveMaxChars`, `parentArchive`, `expandDigestChars`, `refs`, `maxResultChars`); the install keys are refused. Switch from the sidebar's `[profile]`, the dialog's `Switch profile...`, or `/context profile auto|base|`. The source repository's `docs/SPEC.md` has the full table and the behavior. The update check is the only network call the plugin makes, and it runs in the TUI, not in a request: at most one `GET` of this repository's `package.json` per 24 hours, then a toast when the published version is newer than the loaded one. Nothing about it is sent to the model. `"updateCheck": false` in the user file switches it off. ## Use - The model writes memory with the `smart_context` tool: `patch`, `read`, `stats`, `compact`, `ref`, `archive`, `purge`, `recall`, `expand`. - A turn that left the working window is readable before it is archived: `expand` looks in the archive first and then in the pending queue, and says when a read is not durable. `archive` without `keepRaw` warns that the raw is now gone, so `expand` can only return the gist. - A subagent can read its spawning session's archive without importing it: `recall`/`expand` with `from:"parent"`. The field is read-only and never reaches a writing action, and the reply tells the child how many characters its caller can actually keep. - `/context` prints the current memory and archive, and carries the control actions a user needs; the subcommands are in [The `/context` command](#the-context-command). - The palette command `Context status` opens the same numbers as a dialog, with `Switch profile...`, `Resume` and `Purge a turn...` below them, and the TUI sidebar carries a short block of the same numbers with clickable `status` / `profile` / `resume` / `purge`; see [The TUI status dialog](#the-tui-status-dialog). - `/undo` is followed: when the host commits a revert, the plugin rolls its own record back with it - memory written in the undone turn is undone, notices it retired are pinned again, purged turns come back, and the memory block says so for that turn. The journal covers the last eight turns; see "Undo" in the SPEC. Every request starts with a `` block. If `goal` is empty, the model is told to write the request there before the raw first message leaves the working window. In the append layout, that block is a checkpoint; a completed turn that wrote memory carries a `` delta, and a `` note after the current turn carries the mode and the shared pool. ## The `/context` command `/context` is the user's window into the same state the model sees. It prints; it does not edit the memory document - the model stays the only writer of the semantic content. | Command | Effect | | --- | --- | | `/context` or `/context status` | the status report: its first line names the product and the loaded build, the second names the profile in force and the model, then memory and working usage against their caps, turns kept and dropped, `over budget`, the goal, the host system size (display only), the pinned notices, the pending evictions and the archive | | `/context now` | archive every pending turn immediately, instead of waiting for an eviction to age it | | `/context resume` | start a model turn with the plugin's resume cue through the host's synthetic channel - no user message, no new turn, and no pending eviction aged | | `/context profile` | print the profile in force (name, how it was chosen, the model), every named profile with its overrides, the model mappings and the default | | `/context profile auto\|base\|` | pin this session to a named profile, pin it to the base config, or clear the pin so the model mapping and the default decide again | | `/context memory ` | print one memory key as JSON: `goal`, `plan`, `facts`, `files`, `decisions`, `open`, `refs` or `notes` | | `/context recall ` | search the archive for a term; lists matching turn ids and gists, marking an entry `(gist only)` when its raw messages are gone | | `/context purge ` | delete one pending or archived turn by id | An unknown subcommand prints the usage line. Apart from `resume`, a `/context` reply arrives as a real user turn, so it counts toward the working window and can age a pending eviction. After `/undo`, the status report adds two lines: `last undo:` (the boundary turn it rolled back to, how many memory keys were restored, how many turns were dropped, and a `not restorable` count when the journal could only do part of the job) and `undo journal:` (how many turns `/undo` would roll back now, and the oldest one it still covers). ## The TUI status dialog `Context status` (palette id `mega-smart-context.status`) shows the same numbers as `/context` without spending a turn: memory and working usage against their caps, turns kept and dropped, pending/archive/ref counts, and the host system size when the last pass measured one. It is a pull - one call when you run the command, nothing rendered continuously, and no request ever made from a render path. Below the numbers are three actions: | Action | Effect | | --- | --- | | `Switch profile...` | pick `auto`, `base` or a named profile for this session. `auto` follows the model mapping and then the default; a manual pick stays until you pick `auto` again | | `Resume` | the same cue `/context resume` sends, through the host's synthetic channel - no user message and no new turn | | `Purge a turn…` | lists the pending and archived turns, asks which one, confirms, then deletes it from the record. Journaled like the tool's purge, so `/undo` can put it back | The two halves of the plugin keep separate stores, so the dialog reads the session record over the host's plugin RPC (`stats`, `purge`, `notice`, `profile`). If the host has no RPC bridge, or the open route is not a session, the dialog says why instead of failing; an RPC error is reported the same way. The command id is the keybind key if you want a shortcut - no default binding is claimed. A first install may need a restart before the command appears. ### The sidebar block The same numbers also sit in the TUI sidebar, appended to `sidebar.content` so they are the last item in its scrollable list: a header of the plugin name with the loaded version against the block's right edge, the profile in force under it (`profile lean · auto`), a memory bar, a working-window bar, turns kept and dropped, pending/archive/ref counts, and how old the numbers are (`measured 6m ago`). The age line took the slot the host system size used to occupy - the size is outside the plugin's budget and the glance cannot act on it, while an old number tells you the block is not current. The header and both bar lines are spread to that same right edge, so the sidebar's own width decides where the version and the numbers land and a wider pane widens the gap rather than the bar; each bar is eighteen cells. The bars' numbers are right-aligned to a shared column so the slashes line up, and an over-cap working line carries a `*` in the gutter before its value. Gists, notice text and the archive list stay out - the block never grows with the session. Under it are `[status]` (opens the dialog), `[profile]` (the picker), `[resume]` (asks first, then sends the cue) and `[purge]` (the same list and confirmation as the dialog). Each acts when the mouse button is released, so the dialog a click opens is not dismissed by that same release. The block renders from a per-session mirror that is pulled once when the session is shown, once after each idle pass, and again after a purge; at most one pull per session is in flight, a repeat inside fifteen seconds is skipped, and the mirror keeps the thirty-two most recent sessions. Renders never call the RPC. If the slot API or the JSX runtime is missing the dialog still works, and its `sidebar:` row says `unavailable`; `"sidebar": false` turns the block off. ### The session panel `Context panel` (palette id `mega-smart-context.panel`) opens the full report in the host's session panel: both budgets, the request's own system-prompt size, the goal, a sparkline of the last forty passes, every pending and archived turn with `[purge]`, the pinned notices with `[retire]` on the superseded ones, and the undo state. The newest notice is the live instruction and has no retire action. The footer offers `[refresh] [resume] [dialog] [close]`. Purge and retire ask first, write through the same RPC, then refresh the shared mirror. It is independent of `sidebar`: the block's setting only skips the block's own claim. A host without the panel API reports `panel: unavailable` in the dialog. ## Installer `scripts/install.ts` copies the shippable set (`package.json`'s `files[]` plus `package.json`) into: - user: `~/.config/opencode/plugins/mega-smart-context` - project: `/.opencode/plugin/mega-smart-context` It is idempotent by content hash: an in-sync copy is left alone; a drifted copy is resynchronized. `--status` reports missing, changed and extra files. It never copies `node_modules`. ## Checks ```sh npm install npm run typecheck # tsc --noEmit, strict npm run smoke # the context pass: memory injection, the working window, the archive npm run test:install # the installer's copy/drift/remove assertions npm run analyze # read a recorded session back: enabled payload vs the disabled baseline ``` ## Where the details live - [`docs/SPEC.md`](docs/SPEC.md) — the user-visible behavior in full. - [`docs/features/`](docs/features/index.html) - the feature map for this plugin itself: the handoff, the memory tool, the archive, subagents, refs, compaction, the install, the analyzer, and the terminal half (status dialog, sidebar block and update toast). - [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) — how to work on the plugin. - [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md) — where things currently stand. ## Buy me a coffee This plugin is free and MIT-licensed. If it earns its keep, you can [buy me a coffee via PayPal](https://www.paypal.me/mega3dp). ## License MIT — see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). Copyright (c) Evert Chin

# Session handoff - mega-smart-context

Next: `docs/features/index.html` - the feature map. Read only the page for your area before the code.

**A snapshot, not a source of truth.** This file goes stale by design. If it disagrees with the code, the code is right. The process doc is `AGENTS.html`, the feature map is `docs/features/` and the behavior spec is `docs/SPEC.html`. This file is the volatile one - it exists so a new session knows *where things stand*, not *how they work*.

As of `main` (the append layout ships behind `contextLayout`) - 2026-11-14.

## State

- **Compaction is now a commit window with a 20k tail (11/18).** A full pool raises `compact.due` with the current turn recorded; the state note lists the turns that will leave, and the fold waits for the next prompt (or `action:"compact"`), so the model has the whole turn to write what matters into memory. The fold keeps the newest `compactKeepTokens` (20k default, a new session key) of turns and archives the rest immediately with raw kept. The Deck Tracker audit had shown why: the old fold kept a 500k-token working-share tail that freed nothing, and the model purged 29 leaving turns instead of summarizing them. Smoke 577 pins the commit window, the leaving list, the fold-at-next-prompt and the straight-to-archive path; the old one-pass fold is gone.

- **The tail state note moved behind the current turn (11/15).** A live audit of four append sessions found the one cache break left: the note prints live pool numbers and sat before the current turn, so every pass inside a tool loop changed a byte ahead of the turn and the provider re-read the whole turn (10-50k uncached tokens per pass; pre-switch snapshot turns paid 1-4k). `buildAppendPlan` now pushes the note after the turn; it is still the last message the model reads. Smoke pins the note's position and that a second pass in one turn leaves the earlier bytes alone. The measurement and the design tour are updated; the TUI `layout: append` line is unchanged.

- **The append layout is live-measured and ships (11/14).** `contextLayout:"append"` keeps the memory block as a checkpoint and appends one accepted delta after each completed turn; compaction is the only routine step that moves the checkpoint. A scripted live session with a 10k-token memory document and one patch per turn measured the difference against snapshot: snapshot re-read the whole memory block on every follow-up request (~9.7k uncached tokens, 52% cache hit), append read it once and then paid only the new bytes (~250 uncached, 98-99% hit), with `base` byte-stable at 40,510 chars across four turns. The same run caught the failure mode: the model compacted unprompted on turn 5, moved the checkpoint and cost the next pass ~900 cached tokens; the tool description now reserves `compact` for a state note that says compaction is due. Branch `feat/append-only-memory` (6771b15 plus this pass), merged into `main`; the installed copy is synced to the branch.

- **Profiles give one session its own budget, chosen by a click or by the model (10/27).** A profile is a named bundle of the eleven session keys (`SESSION_KEYS`: `memoryTokens`, `workingTokens`, `charsPerToken`, `evictionLead`, `autoArchive`, `archiveMaxTurns`, `archiveMaxChars`, `parentArchive`, `expandDigestChars`, `refs`, `maxResultChars`) in `mega-smart-context.json`; the install keys are refused like an unknown key. Selection is a manual pin on the record, then a `modelProfiles` entry for `event.model`, then `defaultProfile`, then the base. The pin is per session and never expires on its own - only picking **auto** clears it, whatever model is used later. The pass stamps `record.lastModel`, so the tool, `/context` and the RPC re-derive the same choice without a request event. `src/core/profiles.ts` owns `chooseProfile`/`applyProfile`/`configForRecord`/`profileSummary`; `config.ts` gained `profiles`/`modelProfiles`/`defaultProfile` (the maps merge across layers; a mapping or default naming a missing profile is a load error); `context.ts` resolves at the top of `buildPayload`; `budgetOf` reports the effective caps. The sidebar gains a `profile lean · auto` line and `[profile]`, the dialog `Switch profile...`, the panel a Budget row, `STATUS_RPC` a fourth method `profile`, and `/context profile [auto|base|<name>]` is the no-TUI path. Smoke 466 -> 512 (+46). Not seen live yet: the TUI render is smoke-only (like every JSX change), and a config edit still needs a reload of the server half.

- **The policy names the one wrong way to call `smart_context` (10/27).** A model in the ODT session wrapped the tool in Code Mode - `tools.smart_context({ action: "archive", … })` inside `execute` - and got `Unknown tool 'smart_context'. Use search to find available tools.` back while the execute call still reported `completed`, so it read as a silent failure. The same wrapper failed in this session too: 25 rows DB-wide across 9 sessions, plus `shell` 22, `feature_map` 9 and `read`/`glob`/`webfetch` 3 each. The registration is `options: { codemode: false }`, and the host's flag is exclusive rather than additive: `false` is a direct tool by name and keeps it out of the Code Mode catalog, while `pinned: true` only keeps a code-mode tool inside that catalog (the host's own `opencode.session_move`/`worktree_*` use it and are still reachable only as `tools.opencode.*`). One flag per tool, and two registrations of one name replace each other, so no host setting makes the wrapper resolve. `POLICY` therefore gained a bullet - call `smart_context` by name, never `tools.smart_context(...)` inside `execute`, and batch independent direct calls in one assistant message - `tool.ts` documents the exclusivity at the flag, the memory-tool page explains it under "Batching calls", and the global `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` carries the same rule for `smart_context` and `feature_map` (the harness's own tool). Smoke 465 -> 466.
- **The bars are longer, and the numbers ride the block's right edge (10/25).** `STATUS_BAR_WIDTH` went 10 -> 18 cells, one constant shared by the sidebar block, the dialog rows and the panel. The budget lines now set `SidebarLine.spread` too, so the numbers sit on the same column as the header's version; `spread` therefore means "the LAST span goes to the right edge, everything before it stays together on the left", drawn in `sidebar.tsx` with a `flexGrow` spacer rather than `justifyContent="space-between"` - a budget line has four spans (label, filled, empty, numbers) and `space-between` would pull the label, the fill and its track apart. `sidebarText`'s flat fallback joins the left spans with nothing and puts one space where the gap sits. Two literal-`10` assertions moved onto the constant, four new ones pin the spread and the shared width: smoke 465. Trap: the opentui JSX types make `Show`'s child parameter implicitly `any`, so it needs an explicit `(span: () => StatusSpan)`. The static docs (tui.html, SPEC.html, README) are updated; the new line is typecheck+smoke only until a client reload, like every JSX change.

- **A stale instance wrote the block and could clobber the store (10/25).** The host loads the server half more than once, and each instance caches its own `SessionRecord`; the one that owned the `stats` RPC answered an ODT session with `win 432k / 40k` from a 07:24 snapshot while the stored record said 3,335 at 07:32. A purge from that instance would have written the 07:24 record back, un-trimming the archive. Now: `SessionStore.load(sessionID, { fresh: true })` skips the cache and replaces it, and the `stats` RPC and `/context` use it; a failed read keeps the cached copy rather than resetting. `save` compares the stored `updatedAt` with the copy it was handed and, when the stored one is newer, refuses, adopts the stored record and logs the stamps; `mutate` loads fresh and retries its callback once on a refusal, then throws `StoreConflictError`, which the tool, `/context` and the `purge`/`notice` RPC turn into a sentence (nothing was written). The guard is a timestamp comparison, not a CAS: two saves in one read-write round trip can still interleave. The sidebar's `host ~4.1k est · not counted` line is gone - its slot carries `measured 6m ago` (`ageLabel`, `statsOf(..., now)`), and the panel adds the same line once a minute has passed without a write. Smoke 461 (+16).
- **A dropped turn is readable before it is archived (10/25).** An evicted turn's raw sits in the record, but `expand` only looked in the cold archive, so a real session that lost a spec got `no archived turn`, guessed the cut-off word, and archived the pending turn gist-only under that guess - the only copy gone. `expand` now resolves the archive first and then the pending queue (`findPending`, exported for that), adds a one-line note that a pending read is not durable and that `keepRaw:true` is what keeps it, and its miss names both places it looked. `recall` stays archive-only. `archive` without `keepRaw` now reports `gist only; the raw was discarded, so expand will show only this gist`, and both `TOOL_HELP` and the tool description the model is shown say the same before the call. The mechanical gist and the pending-eviction preview share `gistText`: first 120 characters plus the last 40, because a head-only 90-char cut is what dropped the decisive word (the tail is where a name, path or verdict lands). Smoke 445 (+15).
- **Only the live mode stays pinned (10/25).** A Plan and a Build reminder can never both be in force, and the host re-emits them instead of withdrawing one, so "pin every distinct text" left the superseded mode sitting in the block. A real session showed the cost: after a switch to Build the pin held the Build reminder dated by its first sight (two days old) and then the 468-byte Plan block dated later, and the model read the stale "do not implement, tell the user to switch agents" as the instruction and refused to edit. `upsertNotices` now retires the older of the pair into the same `record.retired` list the model writes (`collapseModeNotices`, classified by `modeReminderOf` on the `<system-reminder>` shape), so the copy still in the window cannot resurrect it; a re-emission of that mode returns it and retires the other. The output-limit nudge is deliberately outside the pair. Both the stored `id` and the heading's date now follow the newest occurrence, so a reminder emitted a minute ago no longer reads "seen 2026-10-20". Smoke 430.
- **The terminal half is verified live, and a delegate read a real archive (10/25).** After a client restart the user confirmed all three surfaces in a real TUI: the sidebar block renders (two-edge header, aligned meters, the `*` in its gutter), the palette command's panel row opens the full report, and every click target fires. ## Known gaps (volatile; the durable traps live in the feature pages)

- **The smoke is not the host.** It exercises the transform, the tool, the archive, subagents, compaction and the installer through a fake `ctx`. The live run found one shape mismatch the fake host hid (`content` tool results); assume other shapes can differ too.
- **`/context` delivers through `ctx.session.prompt`.** That creates a user message, which the next context pass treats as a real turn. It does not corrupt memory, but the command's report can become part of the conversation it is reporting on. There is no display-only channel: `ctx.session.synthetic` still starts a model turn (probed live), so `prompt` is the honest choice.
- **A child's archive survives until the store's LRU evicts it** (`MAX_SESSIONS` 64). There is no per-child cleanup on session end. The startup sweep only removes records whose session the host no longer has; records for sessions that still exist are never capped on disk.
- **The archive caps are per session** (`archiveMaxTurns`, `archiveMaxChars`); there is no global storage budget.
- **The ref reader uses the session directory's `docs/features/`.** A bare page name tries `<name>.html` then `<name>.md`; an explicit extension tries that file first and its sibling second. An HTML page is flattened to Markdown-shaped text (`htmlToText`), so `extractSection` runs over either format; `refs.md` written by an old session still finds `refs.html`. The loaded build contains it (v0.1.18) and it is exercised live (10/21): a ref against a `###` chunk of `context-handoff.html` resolved (153 est against a 29-est gist). A ref taken while the page is being written fails the same way and expands when re-stored. A worktree without that directory reports "section not found" but still stores the pointer.
- **The install is a copy.** Editing the source tree does not update an installed copy; run `plugin:install` again, and the host picks it up at the next pass. `plugin:status` reports the drift.
